title: STOPP-relevant medicines for older-adult review
description: Repository-ready UK-focused file for flag-plus-context STOPP display. Entries are intended to flag STOPP-relevant medicines and explain the criterion context; they are not automatic determinations that a STOPP criterion is definitively met.

approach.uiInstruction: Flag STOPP-relevant medicines and show criterion context. Do not automatically label criterion met unless structured context is available.
approach.reviewNotice: Any output should be reviewed against the clinical record, indication, dose, formulation, duration, frailty, co-morbidity, renal function, falls risk, and current local or national guidance before use in practice.

schema.name: Generic medicine name used for matching.
schema.aliases: Common UK brand names or alternate spellings.
schema.stoppRelevant: Boolean; true when the medicine should trigger a STOPP-relevant flag.
schema.criterionSummary: Plain-language summary of the STOPP-relevant criterion or review rule.
schema.whyItMatters: Why the medicine is relevant in older adults.
schema.contextToCheck: List of clinical questions needed to interpret the flag.
schema.sourceType: Usually STOPP or STOPP-related review prompt.

medicines.name: diazepam
medicines.criterionSummary: Benzodiazepines for at least 4 weeks are potentially inappropriate in older adults.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with prolonged sedation, confusion, impaired balance, falls, road traffic accidents, and dependence or withdrawal risk.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this has been prescribed for 4 weeks or longer and whether risks now outweigh benefits.

medicines.name: lorazepam
medicines.criterionSummary: Benzodiazepines for at least 4 weeks are potentially inappropriate in older adults.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with sedation, confusion, impaired balance, falls, and dependence or withdrawal risk.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this has been prescribed for 4 weeks or longer and whether risks now outweigh benefits.

medicines.name: temazepam
medicines.criterionSummary: Benzodiazepines for insomnia for at least 2 weeks, and benzodiazepines used for at least 4 weeks overall, are potentially inappropriate in older adults.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with dependency, next-day sedation, falls, fractures, and reduced ongoing benefit.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this has been used for insomnia for 2 weeks or more, or overall for 4 weeks or more.

medicines.name: nitrazepam
medicines.criterionSummary: Benzodiazepines for insomnia for at least 2 weeks, and benzodiazepines used for at least 4 weeks overall, are potentially inappropriate in older adults.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with prolonged sedation, falls, confusion, and dependence.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this has been used for insomnia for 2 weeks or more, or overall for 4 weeks or more.

medicines.name: zopiclone
medicines.criterionSummary: Z-drugs for insomnia for at least 2 weeks are potentially inappropriate in older adults.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with falls, fractures, next-day sedation, and limited sustained sleep benefit.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this has been used for insomnia for 2 weeks or longer and whether it is still helping.

medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this has been used for insomnia for 2 weeks or longer and whether it is still helping.

medicines.name: quetiapine
medicines.criterionSummary: Antipsychotics for behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia for longer than 12 weeks are potentially inappropriate unless symptoms are severe and non-pharmacological measures have failed.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with stroke, myocardial infarction, sedation, and falls in older adults.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this is being used for BPSD for more than 12 weeks and whether ongoing treatment is still justified.

medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this is being used for BPSD for more than 12 weeks and whether ongoing treatment is still justified.

medicines.name: omeprazole
medicines.criterionSummary: A proton pump inhibitor at full therapeutic dosage for more than 8 weeks may be potentially inappropriate unless there is a continuing clear indication.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with unnecessary long-term exposure, adverse effects, and avoidable polypharmacy.
contextToCheck: Previous ulcer or GI bleed history
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether full-dose treatment has continued beyond 8 weeks and whether a lower dose or stopping is appropriate.

medicines.name: ibuprofen
medicines.criterionSummary: NSAIDs may be potentially inappropriate in older adults in the presence of peptic ulcer disease without gastroprotection, significant hypertension, heart failure requiring loop diuretic therapy, or impaired renal function.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with GI bleeding, renal injury, worsening blood pressure, and heart failure decompensation.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this NSAID is being used in a high-risk setting such as ulcer history, renal impairment, or heart failure.

medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with GI bleeding, renal injury, CNS adverse effects, and worsening heart failure or blood pressure control.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this NSAID is being used in a high-risk setting such as ulcer history, renal impairment, or heart failure.

medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this NSAID is being used in a high-risk setting such as ulcer history, renal impairment, or heart failure.

medicines.name: morphine
medicines.criterionSummary: Regular opioid treatment in older adults warrants review, especially if constipation prevention, sedation monitoring, and falls assessment are lacking.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with constipation, sedation, falls, and delirium risk.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether regular opioid treatment is still needed and whether bowel care and sedation monitoring are in place.

medicines.name: oxycodone
medicines.criterionSummary: Regular opioid treatment in older adults warrants review, especially if constipation prevention, sedation monitoring, and falls assessment are lacking.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with constipation, sedation, falls, and delirium risk.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether regular opioid treatment is still needed and whether bowel care and sedation monitoring are in place.

medicines.name: tramadol
medicines.criterionSummary: Regular opioid treatment in older adults warrants review, especially if constipation prevention, sedation monitoring, and falls assessment are lacking.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with constipation, sedation, falls, delirium risk, and serotonergic adverse effects in some contexts.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether regular opioid treatment is still needed and whether bowel care and sedation monitoring are in place.

medicines.name: furosemide
medicines.criterionSummary: Loop diuretics may be potentially inappropriate when used for dependent ankle oedema alone or as monotherapy first-line treatment for hypertension in the absence of heart failure.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with dehydration, electrolyte disturbance, and avoidable prescribing when indication is weak.
contextToCheck: Whether used for ankle oedema alone
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether there is a clear indication such as heart failure or clinically significant fluid overload.

medicines.name: digoxin
medicines.criterionSummary: Digoxin may be potentially inappropriate as first-line treatment for atrial fibrillation rate control or at higher doses in older adults, especially with impaired renal function.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with toxicity risk, especially in renal impairment and older age.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether digoxin is being used at an appropriate dose and for a clear indication.

medicines.name: aspirin
medicines.criterionSummary: Aspirin may be potentially inappropriate depending on dose, indication, bleeding risk, and antithrombotic combination therapy.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with GI bleeding and avoidable harm when indication is unclear or when combined inappropriately with other antithrombotics.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether aspirin is clearly indicated, at an appropriate dose, and not part of an unnecessary high-risk combination.

medicines.name: clopidogrel
medicines.criterionSummary: Clopidogrel may be potentially inappropriate depending on indication, duration of combination therapy, and bleeding risk.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with avoidable bleeding harm when continued unnecessarily or combined inappropriately with other antithrombotics.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether clopidogrel remains indicated and whether combination antithrombotic therapy duration is appropriate.

medicines.name: warfarin
medicines.criterionSummary: Anticoagulants may be potentially inappropriate depending on bleeding risk, indication, monitoring, and concurrent antiplatelet therapy.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with major bleeding risk if monitoring, dose adjustment, or co-prescribing review is inadequate.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether anticoagulant treatment remains appropriate and whether bleeding risk and co-prescribing have been checked.

medicines.name: apixaban
medicines.criterionSummary: Anticoagulants may be potentially inappropriate depending on bleeding risk, indication, renal function, and concurrent antiplatelet therapy.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with major bleeding risk if dosing or co-prescribing review is inadequate.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether anticoagulant treatment remains appropriate and whether dosing and co-prescribing have been checked.

medicines.name: rivaroxaban
medicines.criterionSummary: Anticoagulants may be potentially inappropriate depending on bleeding risk, indication, renal function, and concurrent antiplatelet therapy.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with major bleeding risk if dosing or co-prescribing review is inadequate.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether anticoagulant treatment remains appropriate and whether dosing and co-prescribing have been checked.

medicines.name: simvastatin
medicines.criterionSummary: Statin treatment may require review in older adults depending on whether it is being used for primary or secondary prevention, and according to frailty and life expectancy.
medicines.whyItMatters: May represent low-value treatment in some contexts, while remaining important in secondary prevention.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether ongoing statin treatment remains beneficial in the current clinical context.

medicines.name: atorvastatin
medicines.criterionSummary: Statin treatment may require review in older adults depending on whether it is being used for primary or secondary prevention, and according to frailty and life expectancy.
medicines.whyItMatters: May represent low-value treatment in some contexts, while remaining important in secondary prevention.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether ongoing statin treatment remains beneficial in the current clinical context.

medicines.name: amitriptyline
medicines.criterionSummary: Tricyclic antidepressants may be potentially inappropriate in older adults because of anticholinergic burden, orthostatic hypotension, and falls risk.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with confusion, constipation, urinary retention, postural hypotension, and cardiac effects.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether a tricyclic remains necessary and whether its anticholinergic or falls risks outweigh benefits.

medicines.name: dosulepin
medicines.criterionSummary: Tricyclic antidepressants may be potentially inappropriate in older adults because of anticholinergic burden, orthostatic hypotension, and falls risk.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with confusion, constipation, urinary retention, postural hypotension, and cardiac effects.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether a tricyclic remains necessary and whether its anticholinergic or falls risks outweigh benefits.

medicines.name: chlorphenamine
medicines.criterionSummary: First-generation antihistamines may be potentially inappropriate in older adults because of sedation and anticholinergic effects.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with confusion, sedation, urinary retention, constipation, and falls.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether a less sedating and less anticholinergic alternative would be safer.

medicines.name: cyclizine
medicines.criterionSummary: Sedating or anticholinergic antihistamine-type medicines may be potentially inappropriate in older adults depending on indication and burden.
medicines.whyItMatters: Associated with confusion, sedation, and cumulative anticholinergic burden.
medicines.plainLanguagePrompt: Review whether this antiemetic remains necessary and whether anticholinergic burden is acceptable.
